summary.text: The hero for whom Tarentum and its river were named — said to be a son of Poseidon by a nymph of the Italian country, in the colonial legend that Phalanthus' Spartan settlement later adopted.

story.text: After Phalanthus seized Tarentum from the barbarians, Pausanias records the local story that Taras the hero was born to Poseidon and a nymph of the country, and that both the city and the river flowing beside it were called after this hero.

At Delphi, among the Tarentine offerings from spoils taken from the Peucetii, Pausanias saw a statue group where the hero Taras stands near Phalanthus of Lacedaemon and a dolphin — recalling how, before Phalanthus reached Italy, a dolphin is said to have brought him ashore after shipwreck in the Crisaean sea.
